title: Personnel of Milton Larkin's band
summary: Cobb names trumpeters, trombonists, bassist, drummer and reed players who passed through Larkin's band and what became of them.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Well, who was the other trumpet players?
Oh, yeah, I know who you mean; he's in Chicago.
He's not a bad trumpet player.

And we had a guy that loved Roy Eldridge -- I'm trying to think of his name; he's in California right now. Coco Guru, we called him. Eddie Hutchinson. He was in that, and he could play. Lester Patterson out of Beaumont -- he's dead now. Then we had on trombone Willie Tomkins, who took Tommy [LIGHT] Young's place in the Luntzwood band, but didn't stay long on account of he couldn't get -- it was during the war days and he couldn't get living accommodations, because he wanted to bring his wife up, and if he couldn't bring his wife up, he quit the band. He stayed one month. And come back and went into the postal service until he retired. He's retired today.

And, on the reed section, well, I told you, Wild Bill Davis was in that band. On the bass, we had Lawrence Cato. He's dead today. We had Doe Mills, who is Henry Mills, out of Shreveport, Louisiana on drums, and he's in Detroit today -- he's doing fine.
Henry Mills. They called him 'Doe' for a nickname. He's in Detroit.
And in the reed section, we had Tom Archer.
Right here in Houston. His niece is Mercer Ellington Anita Moore, who sang with the (UNINTELLIGIBLE) band, but now is with Duke.
But I heard some records, heard very little of him, there was, but he was pretty good.
Yeah, he lived in Chicago for awhile, but he just passed a couple, well, was it last year? I can't keep up with it all -- it was either last year or the year before last, we buried him here.
